rationale:
Positives: The agent authenticated the user properly via full name + zip, acted only on that user’s order, sought explicit confirmation before attempting an order-changing action, and, after the user chose to cancel the entire order, executed the cancellation and provided confirmation. The user’s final intent (cancel the order) was fulfilled.

However, there are two issues that trigger the fail criteria:
- The agent asserted, “You can cancel this item from your order,” which was unsupported by the system. Their subsequent tool attempt failed, and they then admitted individual item removal wasn’t possible. This constitutes stating unsupported information before verifying capabilities.
- The refund amount ($1166.98) and timeline were stated without visible support in the tool output provided (the tool response was truncated in the transcript). While it’s plausible the tool returned this internally, in the provided logs we cannot verify it, so part of the final information appears unverified.

Given the policy’s fail conditions include stating unsupported information, the conversation does not meet the pass bar despite the ultimately correct cancellation outcome.
